name: Sarah Anne Curzon
credit: Portrait of Sarah Anne Curzon, Godey's Magazine (July 1897) · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Sarah Anne Curzon (1833–1898) was an English-born Canadian writer and advocate of women's suffrage, who lived in Toronto.
She wrote the poem and play Laura Secord, the Heroine of 1812 (1887). One of the poets chosen by W. D. Lighthall for Songs of the Great Dominion (London, 1889), an anthology of Canadian verse.

poems.title: The Loyalists
poems.author: Sarah Anne Curzon
poems.text:
O YE, who with your blood and sweat
Watered the furrows of this land,
See where upon a nation's brow,
In honour's front, ye proudly stand !

Who for her pride abased your own,
And gladly on her altar laid
All bounty of the older world,
All memories that your glory made.

And to her service bowed your strength,
Took labour for your shield and crest ;
See where upon a nation's brow.
Her diadem, ye proudly rest !
